A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original SAE feature measurements, CLAP evaluations, layer-probing results, an 80-participant labeling study, and steering experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds a steering listening study and measurements of feature co-activation across models, layers, and SAE configurations.

M1.justification: The activation extraction, top-k SAE architecture and reconstruction objective, feature filtering, top-10 example selection, labeling pipeline, and decoder-vector steering procedure are unchanged. The Essentia specifications newly documented in Appendix D do not establish an underlying method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MusicSet and its constituent corpora for musical concept discovery and retain the 'Simple melody' steering scenario. The added co-activation analysis and listening study assess existing features and steering outputs; no new corpus, musical domain, or input condition is reported.

E2.justification: The new listening comparison in Section 4.6 adds random-direction, matched-norm steering alongside SAE steering and the unsteered baseline. The Essentia/Gemini labeling comparison and the four Gemini variants evaluated in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds two substantive evaluation designs: target matching by 10 listeners, each judging 10 clip sets sampled from the top 50 steerable features, and systematic co-activation measurement using overlap between features' top-10 activating tracks. The latter distinguishes comparisons across layers, SAE configurations, and models. These supplement the retained experimental settings rather than revise them.

E4.justification: New Appendix C investigates concept recovery across independently configured SAEs, cross-layer relationships, and differences between co-occurrence frequency and strength, with case studies and Figures 10–12. The listening study also adds a random-direction control for feature-specific steering. These substantially extend the earlier feature-yield, layer, and captioner analyses.

E5.justification: Section 4.6 newly reports a chi-square significance test for listening choices: chi-square = 48.02, p < .0001. Existing probe uncertainty values and figure uncertainty displays are retained; no increased repeated-run count or revised seed practice is reported.

E6.justification: V3 adds listening outcomes of 66/100 choices for SAE steering versus 17 each for unsteered and random-direction outputs. Appendix C adds extensive overlap results, including 40,490 cross-layer co-occurrence pairs and examples with 40–50% overlap. Tables 1–2 and the results displayed in Figures 1–9 remain unchanged; these are additional findings, not improved scores for retained experiments.

T1.justification: The SAE equations, sparsity projection, activation and filtering definitions, and steering equation are retained. The new overlap analysis supplies an empirical measurement procedure and conceptual interpretations, without adding formal theoretical results, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution explicitly specify autoregressive music models where v2 used broader generative-music wording. The central claims about unsupervised discovery, scalable labeling, familiar and uncodified concepts, and proof-of-concept steering remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds tentative explanations involving robust concept recovery, possible semantic hierarchies across layers, and compression-related differences between early and late representations. It explicitly distinguishes these observations from mechanistic findings and identifies unexplored overlap-threshold sensitivity. Existing music-theory and text-conditioning limitations are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix D identifies six Essentia taggers and their embedding dependencies. It specifies a top-three default, top-four Instrument-Jamendo tags, and top-two Moods-Audioset tags, refining v2's generic description. Hardware details, participant instructions, Gemini prompt/schema, and the project address are retained despite relocation or reformatting.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 and the bibliography add Gujral et al. (2025) on protein-language-model SAEs alongside the retained Simon and Zou work. This is a limited related-work addition; the broader positioning against supervised probing and predefined concepts remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording edits, updates the publication header and author superscripts, adds appendix pointers, and reorganizes appendices around the new co-activation and Essentia sections. The main narrative and most existing prose remain unchanged rather than being extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figures 10–12 add a substantial set of visual analyses: pair-count charts, overlap-strength distributions, configuration comparisons, and a layer-pair heatmap. Existing Figures 1–9 retain their graphics, while Table 1 and Figure 7 move and the Gemini prompt/schema layout is reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 supported steering mainly through CLAP measurements and examples. V3 adds perceptual validation against a matched-norm random-direction control, improving support for meaningful steering, and documents the Essentia pipeline more precisely. Co-activation analyses also extend the evidence about feature organization. The overall gain is limited: the listening study involves 10 participants and selected top features, while the co-activation interpretations remain observational and the central discovery results are unchanged.
